projects.title: Aced Xtrades — Crypto Exchange App
projects.summary: Launched a crypto & gift card exchange in six months with a team of 12, reaching $350K+ in transaction volume and a 45% retention increase.

blocks.text: AcedXTrades is a mobile-first crypto and gift card exchange platform targeting the Nigerian and African market. As founder and PM, I led the end-to-end product lifecycle — from initial ideation and product vision through to launch and ongoing iteration. The platform enables users to buy, sell, and trade cryptocurrencies and gift cards with a focus on speed, trust, and liquidity.

Nigerian crypto and gift card traders were largely served by informal vendors, often over WhatsApp. Trades involved delays and risk, pricing varied from vendor to vendor, consistent liquidity was hard to find, and there was little to guarantee a vendor would honour a deal.
The opportunity was a trusted, mobile-first exchange that made trades fast and predictable, confirmed every outcome, and put more than one financial service in the same app.

items: Defined product vision, feature roadmap, and prioritization framework
Translated requirements into PRDs and user stories for engineering team
Designed user flows for crypto trading and gift card exchange
Managed UI/UX iterations for onboarding and trading experience
Coordinated cross-functional team: developers, designers, marketers, media
Drove partnerships and go-to-market execution
Ran a standing feedback loop with a **6,000+** member community and used RICE scoring to rank what to fix first
Defined product requirements around third-party dependencies, including liquidity and API partner integrations
Negotiated delivery timelines with developers (evidence below)

blocks.text: I shaped Aced Xtrades as a mobile-first exchange built around speed and trust: buy, sell and receive crypto, trade gift cards and pay bills in one app, with clear confirmation of every outcome. What went into each release was decided by community feedback, scored with RICE, so effort went to the friction points users actually reported.
For the V2 revamp I wrote product principles into the PRD, including speed beats aesthetics, clarity over optionality, and never leave users guessing.

items: **$350K+** in transaction volume after launch
**45%** retention increase from structured feedback loops with a 6,000+ member community, prioritized with RICE scoring
**6 months** from start to launch with a team of 12
**Delivery milestone:** V2 revamp PRD and a seven-phase roadmap completed (a planned release, not a shipped result)

blocks.text: I wrote the product requirements for a full platform revamp. The redesign addresses identified UX gaps and introduces modern architecture, wallet upgrades, and new feature categories including virtual card payments (Aced Card), merchant crypto checkout (Aced Pay), and in-app crypto education (Aced Learn).
I planned the revamp roadmap through structured phases: design → architecture → implementation → card integration → QA → soft launch → public relaunch.

The revamp PRD targeted specific gaps: too many steps per transaction, weak success and error feedback, and low post-onboarding retention. I defined the success metrics up front: transaction completion rate, average transaction time, Day 7 and Day 30 retention, and support tickets per 1,000 users. These are targets, not results.

projects.title: Agora Marketplace
projects.summary: Shipped the MVP of a digital marketplace with escrow protection in 48 hours and own the product roadmap.

blocks.text: Agora is a digital marketplace built around escrow protection, so a buyer's money is held until the order arrives. The product promise is simple: shop safe, and sellers get paid when they deliver.

Buying from online sellers carries real risk: fraud, goods that never arrive, and payment disputes with no neutral party to settle them. Buyers want to know their money is protected until they receive what they paid for. Sellers want to know they will be paid once they fulfil the order.
The opportunity was a marketplace where that confidence is built into the transaction itself, through escrow and a structured interaction between buyer and seller.

items: **48 hours** to ship the MVP, validating the marketplace concept with live users
Defined core user flows and product requirements before build
Built and deployed the web application via GitHub and Vercel
Own the roadmap and feature prioritization
Turn customer feedback and market research into PRDs for engineering and design
Used AI-assisted development tools and coordinated the implementation from requirements through to deployment

blocks.text: An escrow-centred marketplace. The buyer's payment is held and only released to the seller once the order arrives, and an order timeline shows where each order stands. I scoped the MVP to the two core sides and the escrow order lifecycle so a working version could ship in 48 hours.
The product serves two sides. Buyers get onboarding, orders, notifications, and an account page. Sellers get their own onboarding, a dashboard, product listings, orders, notifications, and payouts.

items: Interviewed **20+ people** and ran market analysis to decide what to build and why
Built the Notion workspace, PRDs, prototypes and the MVP
Run the kanban board and sprint rhythm for a team of **7**
**48 hours** from requirements to a deployed MVP (delivery milestone)
**2** sides in the MVP: buyers and sellers, each with their own onboarding and order flow (product scope)
**7** people on the kanban board and sprint rhythm I run (team)

projects.title: FoodHunt
projects.summary: Product manager for a three-sided food marketplace. Reached 1,000 active users within two months of launch.

blocks.text: FoodHunt is a three-sided marketplace connecting customers, merchants and riders. I owned the roadmap and worked with engineering, design, QA and the business team to keep releases moving across all three experiences.

A food order depends on three parties at once: the customer ordering, the merchant preparing and the rider delivering. Each needs something different from the same order, and fragmented processes made it hard to keep them coordinated, so a miss on one side degraded the experience for the other two.
The opportunity was one platform that gave customers, merchants and riders each a clear experience, with orders and fulfilment flowing between them.

Defined separate user journeys for customers, merchants and riders
Used launch feedback and operational insights to guide product improvements

projects.title: SpaceRestore
projects.summary: Launched a cleaning and restoration business in three weeks and grew it to 150+ paying clients with a 60%+ referral rate.

blocks.text: SpaceRestore is a cleaning and maintenance service business. I treated it like a product: gather requirements from early service users, then iterate on the service offering, pricing, and booking flow based on what they told me.

Customers looking for cleaning and restoration services often face uncertainty about quality, pricing, booking and accountability. It is hard to know what you will get, what it will cost and who is responsible if it falls short.
The opportunity was a structured service experience that makes it easier to discover, book and receive professional cleaning.

projects.title: Kuda Teen Debit Card

meta.label: Role
meta.value: Independent product analysis (not a Kuda role)

blocks.text: This is a product concept case study completed as part of my EntryLevel Product Management Level 1 certification. It demonstrates my ability to apply PM frameworks — from problem discovery through to MVP definition and prototype scoping — in a realistic product context.
The project was set within the Kuda Microfinance Bank ecosystem. All research, prioritization, and design decisions were conducted independently as part of the programme.
This is independent analysis. I am not affiliated with Kuda, and I did not build or manage this product.

Teenagers aged 11–18 in Nigeria need to make offline and online payments but cannot open bank accounts. This leaves them dependent on cash — which creates safety risks, zero parental spending visibility, and blocked access to online marketplaces and digital services.

items: **End Users:** Teens aged 11–18 in urban/semi-urban Nigeria
**Buyers:** Parents aged 28–50 with Kuda accounts
**Key Cities:** Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Enugu, Ibadan, Delta
**Market Signal:** E-payment value grew ₦280T → ₦384T (2024–2025)

blocks.text: Conducted 3 user interviews to validate the problem space. Key validated pain points: cash loss and theft risk, inability to monitor teen spending, difficulty accessing online payments for school subscriptions and e-commerce, and desire for parental controls without full account responsibility.

The interviews pointed the same way: parents want visibility and control, while teens want access to payments. I focused the analysis on the parent-facing management journey, because the parent is the buyer and the person who has to trust the product.

items: Assumptions Mapping
Risk/Importance Graph
Affinity Mapping
Feature Mapping
MoSCoW Prioritisation
T-Shirt Sizing
Value vs Effort Map

blocks.text: A prepaid debit card product that lives inside the Kuda mobile app, requiring no bank account. Teens use the card for purchases; parents top up balances, set spending limits, receive real-time notifications, and can freeze the card instantly — all from the Kuda app.

Each MVP feature traces back to a pain point from the interviews: spending limits and real-time notifications address the lack of visibility, instant freeze addresses cash loss and theft risk, virtual card access addresses blocked online payments, and the funding dashboard keeps control with the parent without needing a full bank account for the teen.

items: Parent-set spending limits per transaction / period
Real-time push notifications for all teen transactions
Instant card lock / freeze from parent dashboard
Virtual card access for online purchases
Parent funding dashboard within Kuda app
Teen one-time spending approval requests

blocks.text: Produced a clickable Figma prototype of the "Teen Card" section within the Kuda app, scoped to the parent-facing management flow — including card setup, spending limits, transaction history, and freeze/unfreeze controls.

An in-depth product teardown of Moniepoint — Nigeria's leading merchant banking and POS payments platform. I evaluated the product across five dimensions, scoring each on a five-point scale, and provided structured recommendations for each gap identified.

This is an independent product analysis. I am not affiliated with Moniepoint, and I did not build or manage this product. It started from my own experience of how frictionless the app felt when receiving a transfer, which made me want to understand the product decisions behind it.

Moniepoint serves informal merchants, agent banking customers and small business owners in tier-2 and tier-3 cities, a segment most Nigerian fintechs treated as secondary. For these users, a traditional bank account typically means an in-branch visit and several working days.

Reliability for merchants: an account that can be activated in under five minutes, a POS terminal delivered within 48 hours, and a merchant toolset that links payments to inventory, sales records and credit access.

items: **Onboarding Design** — Phone number first, USSD OTP for low-connectivity areas, account in under 5 minutes. Built for its actual users.
**Distribution as Strategy** — POS agents across 33 states, Relationship Manager model, 48-hour terminal delivery.
**Moniebook Data Flywheel** — Payments generate transaction data → credit decisions → merchant growth → more transactions. Creates genuine switching costs.
**Customer Support** — No in-app dispute tracker, no proactive notifications, no escalation SLA paths. Recommendation: real-time in-app dispute tracker with status updates.
**Personal Banking Identity** — ₦10 transfer fee vs free competitors, no cross-product rewards. Recommendation: tiered rewards linking merchant activity to personal account benefits.
**Session Stability** — App terminates sessions without warning during active transactions. Recommendation: proactive push notifications for any account restrictions or session changes.

**Incoming-Transfer Alerts** — The business app sends no push notification when a transfer arrives, so merchants must open the app to confirm payment. Recommendation: real-time payment notifications, which are standard across comparable products.

blocks.text: The most important work ahead for Moniepoint is not new features. It is holding the post-onboarding experience, and customer support in particular, to the same standard as the onboarding that precedes it. Customer support is where the trust built by acquisition is most at risk, which makes it the first priority.
